title: Staggered page-writeback and occupancy-smoothing for paged KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Under bursty continuous-batching workloads we observe cascade OOM-like behavior where many KV pages become cold simultaneously and the GPU swap pipeline experiences sharp latencies and long tail spikes. Root causes identified: synchronous page-writeback bursts from multiple allocator workers, tight residency budget enforcement causing coordinated demotions, and lack of a hysteresis window for spillback to host memory.

Goal: Introduce a staggered page-writeback coalescer and an occupancy-smoothing controller to reduce simultaneous page eviction pressure and smooth GPU swap throughput. The approach reduces tail latency and improves OOM resiliency without increasing average memory usage significantly.
acceptance_criteria: P95 generation latency for 1K concurrent streaming requests improves by >= 20% in replicated cluster benchmarks
Out-of-memory events (GPU OOMs and fatal allocations) reduced to zero in stress tests that previously triggered OOMs reproducibly
Canary rollout (10% traffic) shows no regression in token-per-second throughput or error rate for 72h
Unit and integration tests covering writeback coalescer, stagger windows, and soft-residency accounting included
implementation_notes: Introduce a writeback coalescer module in runtime/kv/writeback_manager.cc that accepts page release intents and schedules writebacks into staggered micro-windows (configurable: base_window_ms, jitter, max_coalesce_bytes)

Add occupancy-smoothing controller (runtime/kv/occupancy_smoother) that maintains a soft_residency_budget per shard. Budget changes are rate-limited with exponential backoff and a configurable hysteresis band to avoid flip-flopping
Modify eviction path to emit release intents instead of immediate DMA transfer when (1) peer writeback load > threshold or (2) soft_residency_budget is being reduced
Writeback worker instances execute coalesced transfers and publish progress metrics (bytes_written, pages_coalesced, writeback_latency_ms) to console telemetry
Integrate thermal-aware throttle hook (optional) that increases writeback window when GPU temperature crosses T_hot to avoid exacerbating thermal throttling
Fall-back policy: if writeback queue grows beyond absolute cap, force synchronous flush for oldest pages to guarantee forward progress (prevents deadlock under pathologically low host bandwidth)
testing_plan: Microbench: synthetic KV access pattern generator with Zipfian token affinity and bursts (10ms-500ms) to validate writeback jitter behavior
Cluster perf: run continuous-batching replay of real production traces (seeded from perf/playbacks/2025-01-kv-burst.tar) across 4-node GPU cluster and compare P50/P95/P99 latencies
Chaos tests: throttle host NVMe bandwidth and inject slow DMA to ensure forced synchronous flush path executes cleanly
Regression tests: verify no-memory-leak in writeback coalescer across 24h soak; validate counters and per-page state transitions
E2E: staged canary for customer-facing host with telemetry alarms set for token rate drop > 5% or error-rate increase > 0.1%
rollout_plan: Internal canary: enable for staging clusters, run 72h perf and crash-only tests
Gradual rollout to 10% of runtime-hosted traffic for 48h, monitor writeback queue depth and writeback_latency_ms
If stable, expand to 50% for 72h; then to 100% with runtime-1.22 release
Post-rollout: keep enhanced telemetry retention for 14 days and run automated anomaly detection against historical baseline
